title: K8s resource references as symbol-level edges, not component-level dependencies
context: Kubernetes manifests contain cross-resource references (ConfigMap/Secret names, Service label selectors) that need to be captured in the symbol graph. The question is whether these should be modeled as component-level or symbol-level relationships. Touches invariant(s): con_039cee7367 (Memory hygiene is the agent's job, done without waiting for the human: accept shipped roadmap proposals, settle provenance-repair escalations (apply the true commit or drop), re-anchor or stale findings, and land the resulting capture commits through a PR. Only decisions that need genuine product judgment are queued for the human.).
decision: Use symbol-level "references" edges instead of component-level "depends_on". This choice was driven by empirical evidence: real Helm charts overwhelmingly co-locate a Deployment and its ConfigMap/Secret in the same templates/ directory, where component-level edges would be filtered out as same-component and produce no graph signal at all. Symbol-level edges preserve the relationship even in this dominant layout pattern.
consequences: References contribute to fan_in/fan_out metrics, making cross-resource relationships visible in analysis
Same-directory resource pairs (Deployment + ConfigMap) now produce detectable edges instead of being filtered away
Matches the practical reality of how Helm charts are structured, not an idealized component model
alternatives_rejected: Component-level "depends_on" edges: would be filtered out as same-component in the dominant real-world case where dependent resources share a directory
